task: Audit Git readiness for the three canonical source roots before any Phase 1 implementation work
objective: Determine, without modifying source or Git history, whether each canonical source root is already a Git repository, which repository boundary owns it, whether a private remote exists, whether the working tree contains pre-existing changes, and whether local commit and remote push are safely available for future Codex implementation tasks.
context: The coordination repository lequochung99/OBM-AI-Coordination is working and Codex can commit and push there.
That does not prove the three local source roots are Git repositories or have safe private remotes.
Current implementation scope is Phase 1 only.
Canonical source roots are Platform UI, Platform API, and WPF InstallationV0.
Do not begin fixing Google ID token, administrator authorization, Tenant/POS creation, Pairing Code creation, WpfJwt, or WPF redeem in this audit task.
constraints: Do not add, remove, or change remotes.
Do not checkout, switch, create, delete, reset, rebase, merge, or force-update branches.
Do not clean the working tree.
Do not alter .gitignore, .gitattributes, submodules, worktrees, or repository configuration.
Do not expose credentials, tokens, remote embedded secrets, connection strings, customer data, or private source content in the report.
Redact any credential-bearing remote URL before reporting.
requiredChecksPerSourceRoot: Does the path exist?
Is the path inside a Git worktree?
Exact Git top-level root from git rev-parse --show-toplevel
Whether multiple requested source roots belong to the same Git repository
Current branch or detached HEAD state
HEAD commit SHA
Configured remotes with credential-safe URLs
Whether origin exists
Remote provider and repository name if safely derivable
Remote visibility: Private, Public, or Unverified; do not guess
Upstream tracking branch
Ahead/behind counts where available without mutation
Working tree status using porcelain output summarized without dumping sensitive file contents
Count and categorized list of modified, added, deleted, renamed, untracked, ignored-not-required files
Whether changes predate this audit and therefore must be treated as user/unknown-owned
Presence of nested Git repositories, submodules, or worktrees relevant to the source boundary
Whether a local commit is technically possible, without creating one
Whether push permission is proven, not proven, or blocked; do not perform a write test
Any branch protection or repository-policy information available read-only
Recommended safe commit boundary for future Phase 1 work
requiredCrossRootAnalysis: State whether the three source roots are three separate repositories, fewer shared repositories, or not under Git.
Identify any parent repository that owns more than one source root.
Identify risk of accidentally committing unrelated project changes together.
Identify whether future Phase 1 work should produce one, two, or three source commit SHAs.
Do not recommend creating a new repository until existing boundaries are fully reported.
prohibitedActions: No staging, commit, push, pull, fetch with credential prompts, merge, rebase, reset, checkout, switch, clean, stash, tag, or branch mutation
requiredEvidence: A per-root audit table with PathExists, IsGitWorktree, GitTopLevel, CurrentBranch, HeadSha, OriginPresent, SafeRemoteSummary, Visibility, Upstream, Ahead, Behind, WorkingTreeState, ChangeCounts, NestedRepoOrSubmoduleState, LocalCommitPossible, PushPermissionState, RecommendedBoundary.
Credential-safe command evidence or summarized outputs sufficient to support each conclusion.
Explicit statement that no source files or Git state were modified.
Explicit statement that no push write-test was performed.
Exact blockers and recommended next action for each root.
A cross-root conclusion specifying expected number of future source commit SHAs.
acceptanceCriteria: All three canonical source roots are audited.
Pre-existing dirty working-tree changes are identified and treated as user/unknown-owned.
Remote existence and visibility are reported without guessing.
Push ability is classified as Proven, Not Proven, or Blocked without performing a mutation.
No source or Git state is changed.
A versioned report and handoff are committed and pushed only to the coordination repository.
The report is detailed enough to choose the safe Git setup before Phase 1 coding begins.

reportingPolicy.ifNotPassOnAnyLaterAttempt: Report must be 100% complete and detailed, including every acceptance criterion, root cause, exact evidence, unresolved ambiguity, risk, and next action.
